overview: White declines the Benko with 4.Nd2, aiming for e4 and a quiet development rather than taking b5. Black can play 4...Bb7 or 4...e6 and still has a Benoni-style position. The play is manoeuvring, with Black challenging on the queenside and White building a central pawn.

white_ideas.idea: Build a centre with e4, Ngf3 and g3
Keep an eye on the queenside and the b5 pawn

black_ideas.idea: Hit c4 with ...b4 or ...bxc4 and use the queenside files
Fianchetto the king bishop and aim at the centre

typical_structures.structure: Benoni-style asymmetric centre with queenside tension

character.notes: The pawn is not accepted, so the play is manoeuvring rather than forcing.

gambit.notes: No pawn is taken or sacrificed.

structure.notes: Queenside tension and an undecided centre.

approach.notes: A normal declined line, seen sometimes.

character.reason: Quiet declined lines lead to manoeuvring play.

gambit.reason: The gambit is declined so no pawn is given.

soundness.reason: A quiet sound option for White.

structure.reason: Queenside tension without a settled centre.

approach.reason: A recognised, less common reply to the Benko.

plans.reason: White builds a centre and slowly gains space.
